_note: How a long-form video's runtime actually breaks down. Auto-generated transcripts were cut into ~30-second blocks and each block classified as the presenter's own substance, source material read aloud, filler, or promotion. A one-off sample, not a live feed.
_method: The 12 most recent long-form uploads on TheQuartering that have transcripts, as of 2026-08-07 — 333 blocks of roughly 30 seconds each. Classified per video against a fixed rubric, then a separate pass re-rated 48 blocks drawn from across all 12, shuffled and stripped of surrounding context; it agreed with 79% of the original calls. Every single disagreement was the blind rater marking something as substance where the in-context rater saw source-reading or repetition, so the filler share here is more likely understated than overstated.
_caveat: Substance vs read-aloud is the softest line, because auto-transcripts carry no quotation marks. The combined 'not filler, not promo' share is the firmer number.
